## Our understanding and proposed approach

### What we heard

Kilbride Veterinary Group runs three clinics, in Navan, Trim and Kells, with 11 vets and 19 support staff. Phones are the main pain point. The clinics take roughly 640 inbound calls a week. Orla estimates that about 38% of after-hours calls go unanswered or reach a voicemail nobody checks until morning.

Most calls are routine. About half are appointment bookings and changes. The rest are largely repeat prescriptions and "is this an emergency?" questions.

Emergencies are the one thing that cannot go wrong. Any call that might be an emergency must reach the on-call vet immediately.

### What you want

An assistant that:

- answers calls after hours
- books routine appointments
- sends reminders
- routes anything that might be an emergency straight to the on-call vet's mobile

### Our proposed approach

We suggest a 6-week pilot at Trim, your smallest clinic, before rolling out to all three. A small start lets us test the emergency routing and the booking flow with real calls. We can fix problems before they affect the busier clinics.

You would like the service live before the spring vaccination rush in March 2027. The pilot start date and the rollout dates are to be confirmed.

### Two points we need to settle

**Bookings and VetLink 4.** Orla confirmed that VetLink 4 has no API. That means the assistant cannot write bookings directly into the system. There are two options: a daily export and import, or staff entering bookings by hand. We know this was disappointing. Each option has a cost in staff time and in how current the diary is. We will set both out so you can choose. Which option to use is to be confirmed.

**Call recordings and client data.** Your records include owner names, addresses and phone numbers. Orla asked where call recordings would be stored. We do not yet have an answer and will come back to her on this. Storage location and retention are to be confirmed.

### Still to be agreed

- Budget. Orla will raise this with the two partners.
- How the assistant decides that a call might be an emergency, and how the on-call vet is reached if they do not answer. We would agree this with your vets.
- Pilot start date and success measures.

Subject: Your kitchen installation, order K-2291

Dear Ms Doyle,

I am sorry. You took two days off work and we let you down both times.

Here is what happened.

On 6 November, our scheduler double-booked the fitting team onto another job. That was our mistake. Nobody rang to tell you.

On 7 November, we sent one fitter to start on the carcasses. Your quartz worktops had not arrived from our supplier. The delay was the supplier's, but we knew about it on 5 November. We should have told you then. We did not.

Your new install date is not yet confirmed. We will set it once the worktops arrive. The supplier now says this will be the week of 24 November. I will not give you a firm date until we are sure of it.

I would like to offer you €150 as a goodwill gesture, as a voucher or account credit. Please tell me which you prefer.

On your deposit of €2,400: our policy is that deposits are non-refundable once materials have been ordered. Yours were ordered on 20 October. I cannot promise a refund. I can pass your request to our operations manager, who makes that decision. I will do so today, and we will let you know the outcome. The timing is to be confirmed.

You should also have a named contact for your order. I will confirm that name to you shortly.

Yours sincerely,

Customer Care
Ardee Kitchens

**Subject: Hybrid working policy from 1 January 2027**

Dear all,

Our hybrid working policy starts on 1 January 2027. Here is what applies to you.

**Who it covers**
- Employees whose role can be done partly from home, as agreed with their line manager.
- Employees in their first six months (probation) are not eligible. They work from the office full time.

**Office days**
- Work from the Galway office at least two days a week.
- One of those days must be Tuesday, our team day.
- You agree the second day with your line manager.

**Core hours**
- At home or in the office, you must be available between 10:00 and 15:00.

**Before you start**
Both of these are required:
1. Your line manager approves in writing.
2. You complete the home-office health and safety self-assessment form.

Hybrid working cannot begin until both are done.

**Equipment and costs**
- The company provides a laptop and headset.
- You can claim a one-off home-office allowance of up to €300, paid on receipts. It covers a desk, chair or monitor.
- Travel between home and the office is not reimbursed.
- The company does not pay home utility bills.

**Data**
- Do not print confidential client drawings at home.

**Review**
- The company may review or withdraw hybrid working for any employee or team. It will give four weeks' written notice. Reasons include changing business needs or a drop in performance.

**To be confirmed**

- How to submit receipts for the allowance.
- What applies to roles that cannot be done remotely.

We will share these details separately. If you have questions in the meantime, email hr@corrib-eng.example.

Kind regards,
HR, Corrib Engineering Ltd

**Q3 2026 board summary (July to September)**

**Headline:** Group sales were almost flat, but the margin on them fell. Athlone is the cause.

**Group**
- Revenue was €1,614k, down €16k (1.0%) on Q3 2025.
- Gross margin was 38.6%, down from 40.5%. That is 1.9 points.
- By our calculation, gross profit fell by about €36k (5.5%).

**Stores**
- **Athlone:** Revenue fell €74k (14.0%) to €456k. Margin fell from 40.8% to 36.1%. A national chain opened 2 km away in June. Athlone also discounted more heavily in August to hold footfall. The finance manager says this explains most of the margin fall. By our calculation, Athlone's gross profit fell by about €52k.
- **Mullingar:** Revenue rose €43k (7.0%) to €655k. Margin fell 0.8 points to 40.2%.
- **Tullamore:** Revenue rose €15k (3.1%) to €503k. Margin fell 0.6 points to 38.9%.

Mullingar and Tullamore together added about €15k of gross profit. That covered only part of Athlone's loss.

**Other points**
- There were no one-off items in either year.
- Click-and-collect, launched in May, is included in each store's figures. It is not reported separately.

**To be confirmed**
- The cause of the part of Athlone's margin fall not explained by discounting.
- The cost of the August discounting.
- Whether Athlone's sales will recover, and the outlook for Q4.
- The contribution of click-and-collect.

**Subject: Client portal outage on Friday 14 November**

Dear client,

Yesterday our client portal was unavailable for about six hours. We are sorry for the disruption.

**What happened**
From 08:55, the portal refused connections and browsers showed a security warning. The portal's security certificate had expired. Automatic renewal had been failing unnoticed since October because of a changed setting. We found the cause at 09:20 and renewed the certificate by 10:40. Some users still saw errors for a while. By 14:55 the portal was working fully.

**Your data**
No one gained unauthorised access. The expiry blocked connections. It did not expose any data. Our IT provider has reviewed the logs.

**Uploads**
Four clients' uploads, made between 08:50 and 08:55, did not complete. We have identified those clients. We will contact each one individually by Monday 17 November. They will need to send their documents again.

**Deadlines**
No deadlines were affected. For affected clients, our staff completed the 14 November ROS filing by phone and email.

**What we have changed**
Two members of staff will now get an alert 30 days before any certificate expires.

Who to contact with questions: to be confirmed.

Kind regards,
Feeney & Walsh Chartered Accountants

Subject: Your Brightwash linen contract

Dear [Name],

Thank you for sending this over. I am not a solicitor, so please have one read the full contract before you sign. Here is what the extract says.

**What you are committing to**
- **Length:** 24 months from 1 March 2025. It then renews automatically for 12 months at a time.
- **Notice:** To stop it renewing, you must give written notice at least 90 days before the renewal date. On my reading, that is around the start of December 2026. A solicitor should confirm the exact date.
- **Exclusive supplier:** You must get all linen hire and laundry from Brightwash.
- **Minimum volume:** You pay for at least 900 kg a month, even if you use less.
- **Price rises:** Charges go up every year by CPI plus 3 percentage points, capped at 8%. For example, if CPI were 2%, the rise would be 5%.

**What to worry about**
- The 900 kg minimum could hurt in quiet months. Check it against your real usage. The price per kg is to be confirmed.
- Missing the notice window locks you in for another year.
- Brightwash's liability is capped at what you paid in the previous 12 months.
- Brightwash is not liable for lost business or profit, including from late delivery. If linen arrives late and you lose income, you probably cannot claim it back.

**Not in the extract (to be confirmed)**
- Delivery times or service standards.
- Any right to leave the contract over poor service.
- The starting price per kg.

**What I suggest**
Ask a solicitor, ideally one who handles commercial contracts, to review the whole document. Ask them about negotiating the minimum volume, the price cap, and an exit right for repeated late delivery. Your accountant can help check the costs.

Kind regards,
[Name]

**To:** Managing Director
**Subject:** CRM replacement for 25 users

**Recommendation**
Choose Pipewell, provided Gerard confirms the Xero link works for us before we commit.

**Annual cost**
- Pipewell: €5,400 in licences (€18 × 25 × 12) plus €720 for Zapier (€60 × 12). Total **€6,120**.
- Larchmont CRM: €8,700 (€29 × 25 × 12). Total **€8,700**.

Pipewell is €2,580 a year cheaper. Its figure does not include Ciara's time or ours on the data import. Whether either price includes VAT is to be confirmed.

**Why Pipewell**
- It costs less.
- The contract is monthly, so we can cancel any time. Larchmont needs a 12-month commitment.
- In the two-week trial, 4 of 6 staff preferred Pipewell's interface. 2 preferred Larchmont.
- It can connect to Xero, which Gerard says is essential. The accounts team re-key every invoice today.

**Trade-offs**
- **Xero:** Larchmont has the link built in. Pipewell needs Zapier, which is an extra service to manage. Whether it covers our invoices fully is to be confirmed.
- **Customs-document fields:** Larchmont has a template. With Pipewell, Ciara needs about 3 days to set up custom fields.
- **Data migration:** Larchmont's vendor does it and it is included. With Pipewell we import the CSV ourselves. The effort is to be confirmed.
- **Support:** Pipewell is email only, in business hours. Larchmont offers phone and email in business hours.

**Next steps**
1. Ask Gerard to test the Zapier link to Xero during a Pipewell trial.
2. Confirm VAT, the migration effort and Ciara's availability.
3. If the Xero test fails, Larchmont is the fallback.

Because Pipewell is monthly, the risk of trying it is low. A wrong choice of Larchmont would cost us at least a year.

Reilly Joinery in Cavan makes custom kitchens and wardrobes. It has 14 staff.

The problem was speed. Quotes took about three working days, because the owner priced every job from scratch in a spreadsheet.

We built a quoting template from their last 200 jobs, with standard units and finishes priced in. We then trained the office manager to use it. The work took six weeks and finished in September 2026.

The result: about 70% of quotes now go out the same day.

The other 30% have unusual layouts or bespoke finishes. They still need the owner and take about as long as before.

Fintan Reilly, owner: "Most quotes go out the same day now. Not every job fits the template, and that's fine - those are the ones that need me anyway."

Effect on win rate and revenue: to be confirmed.

If your quotes wait on one person, we are happy to talk.
